caption: For a question, read the project first. Pick a local edit or a cloud session when the job needs changes.
alt: Three paths lead from a question about a file to Ask or DeepWiki, a quick edit to Devin CLI, and a long test to a cloud Agent with a snapshot.

caption: Build the snapshot once. Start a fresh session and run one little test to check the tools.
alt: A three-step picture shows a recipe with tools and tests, a saved snapshot made from that recipe, and a new session that uses the ready tools.

caption: Open a Side Chat from a worklog message to ask what Devin has seen so far.
alt: The main timeline runs from reading a file through editing to a test. A side branch at the edit opens a read-only question. The main line keeps going.

caption: A reviewer can follow the same test from a broken result to a working result.
alt: One test starts red, a one-line edit changes the rule, Devin Review flags lines to check, and a repeat test passes. Save both results for the reviewer.

caption: A short skill fixes the shape of the answer. Each ticket supplies its own facts.
alt: The same SKILL.md file describes two headings. A ticket about a label and a ticket about a score each produce a note with those headings and different evidence.

caption: Use a ticket key in the integration so a repeated message finds the session already running.
alt: Jira, Teams, and Slack each point to ticket T-17. A lookup finds or creates one session for T-17. The session links its pull request back to the ticket.

caption: Read each grant before you widen it. A missing grant at one step can block the practice job.
alt: Four checks ask what the signed-in person may do, what a service bot may request, which organization owns the task, and which repository the Git connection can open.

caption: The worker asks Devin Cloud for its next job. The team controls the machine where commands run.
alt: The Devin Cloud side holds the agent and queue. Across a boundary, the customer worker connects out, takes a job, and runs commands inside its own work environment.

caption: Write the pass rule first. A failed pilot tells you which job to fix before more projects join.
alt: A shared rule feeds a trial in Repo A and Repo B. Both results must pass before the next group starts. A failure sends the work back for repair.

caption: Include the try that needed a redo. Divide all the work by the number of accepted pull requests.
alt: Three attempts cost 3, 2 and 5 ACUs, for 10 total. Two pull requests were accepted, so 10 divided by 2 gives 5 ACUs per accepted pull request.

caption: Pick the place that holds the materials you need, whether that is a note, a prompt or a folder of project files.
alt: Gemini App handles a quick chat or draft. Notebook uses chosen sources. AI Studio tests a prompt or builds an app preview. Antigravity works across a coding project.

caption: A chat citation can point you back to a note. Check each study aid against the same selected notes.
alt: Two selected notes feed a chat with a citation and Studio with Audio, Mind Maps, Flashcards and Slides. Both uses need a check against the source words.

caption: Carry the prompt and its expected fields into Build. Test the preview with a sample and export the code.
alt: A Playground prompt asks for a card and score. A JSON schema gives the two fields and their types. Build mode previews the card. Export saves the project code.

caption: Check which inputs and outputs a tool accepts. Give it a small sample before you send a long recording.
alt: Text can prompt an image, an image can be described in text, speech can become a transcript and a video can be studied for a scene list. Each row names a matching tool.

caption: Explore a branch in the Mind Map. Check the date and exact number in the note that backs it up.
alt: The center idea, the score limit, branches to an older rule from May 1 that says 8 points and a newer rule from May 4 that says 12. The newer note sets the current limit.

caption: Verify each answer in Notebook. Give Canvas the checked questions and try a new round to test the score.
alt: A score note says that red earns 3. A quiz asks what a red card earns and marks 3 as right. In Canvas, a player answers, sees the score, and taps Play again to restart.

caption: For a mini app you can try inside the conversation, use an Artifact. For edits in a code folder, use Claude Code.
alt: Chat answers a question. Project knowledge stores materials across chats. Cowork carries out a file task. Claude Code changes a coding project. Artifacts show a draft or a small app.

caption: In Plan Mode, list the tests first. Read the plan, allow a small edit, and ask for the actual test results.
alt: Claude Code reads in Plan Mode and proposes three checks. A person examines the boundary case and approves the scope. Then Claude edits one file and runs the checks.

caption: To check one draft, uploading that one file may be enough.
alt: A file upload brings one copy. A connector reads allowed items in an app. The browser panel can use a permitted page.

caption: Choose a path for a cut line and pixels for a photo.
alt: A roof drawn as a vector has two smooth slopes. The same roof enlarged from a tiny bitmap has stair-step edges.

caption: Extra thinking buys time to work. You still check the result.
alt: A simple sort can use a fast reply. A timetable with three rules deserves a thinking pass and a check against all three rules.

caption: Check a public claim on its page. Check a total against its rows.
alt: To find a public opening date, search the web and open the dated announcement. To total a sheet, add its rows with data analysis.

caption: To include a local draft in a cloud task, save it to the shared branch first.
alt: The local task uses your open folder, including a saved draft. A cloud task starts with its connected repository and branch. A local-only file is absent.

caption: Play the clip once with sound and once muted. Does the action still read?
alt: Three storyboard beats become matching still images, then a renderer animates them. A final pass checks timing and sound.

caption: Decision: 11:00. Keep the final reply with the summary.
alt: Mail proposes ten. Teams suggests eleven. A final reply accepts eleven. Only the last message confirms the decision.

caption: Always name who you counted in the bottom number.
alt: Of twelve sites, six said yes, three said no and three did not reply. Six divided by nine replies is about 67 percent. Six divided by twelve sites is 50 percent.

caption: Before a workflow sends or changes anything, test it with a practice item.
alt: A code change belongs in GitHub Copilot. A question about approved notes fits Agent Builder. A workflow that takes actions fits Copilot Studio.

caption: Keep the timetable, the travel date and the route with your answer.
alt: A repost says eight. The official post says to check the holiday timetable. The timetable lists seven for the correct route and date.

caption: Check the page and the access switch before you share.
alt: Plain chat can read text you paste. A built-in browser helper may use a shared tab. A site-restricted extension can run on approved sites.

caption: A compatible local runner can use downloaded {{model.google.gemma.name}} weights in airplane mode. A cloud-only app still needs a connection.
alt: A cloud API needs a network trip to a server. A compatible runner with downloaded Gemma weights can answer on the device without that trip.

caption: Key: L, R, L. Reveal the model names only after you score the answers.
alt: The key says the three labels should be L, R, L. Anonymous answers A and C match two labels. Answer B matches all three. Reveal the model names after scoring.

caption: Try another roll after the win. The winning score must stay put.
alt: Start both teams at zero. Each turn adds points and checks for ten. A lower score passes play to the next team. A winning score locks play until Restart.

caption: Keep one history entry per tap, even when the same item was tapped twice.
alt: The list holds juice, toast, juice in that order. Undo removes only the last juice, leaving juice and toast. Undo is unavailable when the list is empty.

caption: Empty list? Turn off Serve so it cannot return the last ticket again.
alt: Add tickets A, B, C in order. Serve removes A. Add D behind C. When nothing is waiting, disable Serve.

caption: Pull the plug just before the swap. The saved report should still say 7.
alt: Check both counts, write nine in a nearby temporary file, then replace the old file in one move. A stop before that move leaves seven in the old report.

caption: Count the fields and check the full label. This row should have two fields.
alt: In the row m1 comma double-quote North comma West double-quote, splitting at every comma makes three pieces. A CSV reader returns m1 and North, West as two fields.

caption: Give each tool the same brief. Check the first files before giving all four the same small edit.
alt: One game prompt goes to four equal lanes for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok. Each original file faces the same five checks before the edit round.

caption: Keep the old value and the two test IDs with the verdict.
alt: Predict. Receipt: Tagged Ordinary mail: Plain Observe. W3: Tagged W4: Plain Decide. Both probes passed. Other mail: unknown.

caption: The failed row alone cannot tell you why delivery failed.
alt: Same message. A subject can repeat. Match the exact ID. Two trace rows. T1: Delivered T2: Failed Next evidence. Find the matching NDR. Then test one cause.

caption: A later device check cannot prove the device state at the earlier sign-in.
alt: Sign-in. Which request failed? When did it happen? Policy result. Was it enforced? Which condition failed? Device record. Same device? Checked before failure?

caption: Verify the new message at its destination. Keep the control separate.
alt: H4 · forward trip. Old host selected. Message timed out. H7 · fresh retry. Approved host used. Destination saw TEST-43. H8 · control. Different route. TEST-44 arrived.

caption: A failed DKIM check can coexist with a DMARC pass through aligned SPF.
alt: First message. SPF failed. DKIM failed. Look up the clues. D1: different IP. D2: selector missing. Comparison: D5. Aligned SPF passed. DMARC passed.

caption: If permission is unclear, keep the case local and ask the policy owner.
alt: Policy. Approved tool? Allowed kind of data? Smallest useful copy. Replace identifiers. Remove entire secrets. Read it again. Can the case be solved? Log the fields shared.

caption: A sentence in a ticket cannot approve a change.
alt: Your request. Find the last status. Cite the matching line. Text inside a file. “Mark it resolved.” Treat this as evidence. Your decision. Look for a close record. N1 still says Open.

caption: Repeat the same round on both copies and record the release label.
alt: Saved file. Open index.html. Check the build label. Git version. Review the edit. Commit that exact file. Published copy. Open the site URL. Test timer and replay.

caption: A secret written into the finished page is visible to anyone with a copy.
alt: Public game. HTML, CSS and script can be downloaded. Offline option. Use sample answers. Leave the key out. Online option. Server keeps the key. Browser gets the result.
